content.rationale: Bottleneck and encoder-space Gaussian distances capture complementary near- and far-OOS deviations. Training-set robust scaling makes their additive fusion comparable without using evaluation-set statistics.

In-scope encoder representations tend to lie near a principal subspace learned from training data, while OOS inputs retain larger orthogonal residuals. Adding a train-calibrated residual score to energy combines representation-space novelty with classifier uncertainty.

The mean distance to a moderately sized neighborhood in normalized encoder space measures local support rather than relying on a single nearest example. OOS queries should have consistently more distant in-scope neighbors.

Low-variance within-class directions encode constraints that in-scope representations satisfy tightly. OOS inputs should produce larger residuals in these trailing covariance directions even when their high-variance coordinates appear plausible.

In-scope representations should have a clearly preferred Gaussian class, whereas OOS queries often have similar distances to multiple classes. A small nearest-versus-second-nearest class distance gap therefore signals geometric class ambiguity.

In-scope examples tend to exhibit class-conditional logit geometry: a characteristic top-two margin and total logit norm. OOS inputs often have atypical confidence shapes, including overconfident but geometrically unusual logits.
L2-normalized in-scope features should align closely with at least one class prototype, while OOS queries are expected to have lower maximum cosine similarity to all learned class directions.

Energy captures classifier uncertainty while full encoder-space Mahalanobis distance measures departure from class-conditional feature support. Train-calibrated ECDF scaling places both signals on a comparable bounded scale without using evaluation-set statistics.

The relative shape of Dirichlet concentrations encodes how evidence is allocated across classes, independently of vacuity or total concentration. OOS inputs should align poorly with the class-specific concentration-shape prototypes learned from in-scope training examples.

Confident predictions retain an energy-dominated score, while samples with unusually uncertain energy receive an additional encoder-space distance penalty. This conditional fusion targets OOS examples whose classifier uncertainty makes representation novelty most informative.

Class-specific diagonal variances retain dimensions that are selectively constrained by individual intents, unlike a tied covariance model. Shrinking each class variance toward the global variance stabilizes rare classes while preserving heterogeneous intent geometry.

The span of class means contains directions that are explicitly discriminative for in-scope intents. OOS inputs should retain unusually large, variance-normalized residual energy outside this supervised subspace.

A ViM-style residual norm measures encoder energy outside the principal in-scope feature subspace, while the maximum logit discounts residuals from confidently supported intents. OOS queries should have both larger residual components and weaker classifier support.

Class-conditional local support in normalized bottleneck space detects queries that may lie near the global in-scope manifold but are poorly supported by examples of their predicted intent. Averaging several neighbors is less sensitive to isolated training points than a single-neighbor distance.

Low-variance within-class directions encode constraints that in-scope bottleneck features satisfy tightly. A predicted-class, shrinkage-stabilized trailing-subspace distance detects violations of those constraints.
A query assigned to an intent should lie near that predicted intent's feature distribution, whereas OOS queries can be confidently assigned yet remain atypical for the assigned class.

Differences between log-partition values at multiple temperatures are shift-invariant summaries of the full logit shape, capturing concentration patterns beyond energy or maximum probability. Class-conditional train calibration flags queries whose temperature response is atypical for their predicted intent.

OOS queries may be assigned a confident class while remaining poorly aligned with that predicted intent's normalized feature prototype. Class-specific training calibration accounts for intents whose in-scope examples naturally have different prototype-consistency levels.

MSP captures classifier uncertainty while full-space Mahalanobis distance captures representation novelty. Train-derived percentile calibration makes their scales comparable, and a noisy-OR fusion emphasizes items anomalous by either signal.

The centered log-ratio transform isolates the relative allocation pattern of Dirichlet concentrations while removing total-evidence magnitude. OOS queries should have less local support among in-scope evidential shape patterns.

A train-calibrated energy gate preserves the energy ranking for confident items, while smoothly replacing it with encoder-space novelty when the classifier's energy is unusually uncertain. This avoids applying representation distance indiscriminately to examples already well supported by the classifier.
Per-intent diagonal residuals retain feature dimensions that are tightly constrained for a specific intent, while classwise empirical tail calibration accounts for differing class spread.
Class-mean directions capture supervised variation that separates known intents. OOS queries should retain a larger fraction of their feature energy outside this discriminative subspace.

Residual energy outside a compact in-scope bottleneck subspace captures ViM-style representation novelty, while train-calibrated energy retains uncertainty information for samples whose residual is less distinctive.

Multi-scale neighborhood distances in L2-normalized encoder space measure both immediate local support and broader manifold support. OOS queries should be farther from in-scope examples at both scales, while the geometric mean reduces sensitivity to isolated neighbors.

Low-variance within-class covariance directions encode constraints shared by in-scope intents. OOS queries should violate these trailing-direction constraints more strongly than typical training examples.

An in-scope query's classifier-predicted intent should usually agree with its nearest class prototype in representation space. OOS queries can be forced into a logit class while lying substantially closer to another intent prototype.

The top-two logit margin measures decisional separation not captured by energy alone. Class-conditional lower-tail calibration flags queries whose predicted intent is supported by an unusually ambiguous logit ordering.
In-scope queries should align closely with the normalized prototype of their predicted intent, whereas OOS queries often have weaker cosine support even when the classifier assigns them confidently.

Energy uncertainty and representation-space novelty provide complementary OOS evidence. Train empirical-CDF calibration puts both scores on a shared percentile scale, and their geometric fusion emphasizes inputs anomalous under both signals.

The normalized Dirichlet concentrations describe evidential allocation across intents independently of total evidence. OOS inputs can have an atypical concentration shape for their predicted intent even when vacuity or energy appears in-distribution.

Confident classifier outputs retain the energy score, while energy-uncertain outputs are rescored by predicted-intent representation atypicality. Class-conditional calibration prevents naturally broad intents from receiving excessive feature-distance penalties.

Predicted-intent diagonal Mahalanobis distance preserves class-specific feature variances that a tied covariance suppresses. Shrinkage toward global variance stabilizes intents with few examples while emphasizing dimensions that are unusually constrained within each intent.

Class-mean directions capture the representation components most useful for separating known intents. After removing those directions, OOS queries should have poorer local support in the remaining nuisance and residual feature geometry.

Bottleneck and encoder densities capture complementary near- and far-OOS departures. Each density is converted to a train-calibrated survival score, then additive weights are fitted from held-out train density reliability.

A query outside the in-scope feature manifold should retain unusually large energy after projection away from the dominant global encoder subspace. Class-conditional train calibration accounts for intents with naturally different residual variation.

Class-conditional k-nearest-neighbour distance in the normalized bottleneck space measures whether a query has local support among examples of the intent assigned by the classifier. OOS queries forced into a known intent should often remain distant from that intent's local representation manifold.

Low-variance within-class directions encode constraints that in-scope examples of an intent should satisfy. Class-conditional neighbor distance in this whitened trailing subspace measures local violations of those constraints.

Queries forced into a high-confidence known intent can still lie unusually far from that predicted intent's representation prototype. Class-conditional tail calibration accounts for natural differences in within-intent spread.

The centered logit norm measures the classifier's overall contrast between intents while removing arbitrary common logit shifts. OOS queries often induce unusually weak class-discriminative logit geometry even when their energy is not extreme.
In-scope queries should align with the normalized prototype of their predicted intent, whereas OOS queries are often assigned a class despite weak cosine prototype support.

Energy captures classifier uncertainty, while trailing-direction residual distance detects violations of low-variance in-scope representation constraints. Train empirical-CDF calibration places both OOS evidences on a shared scale, and their product emphasizes queries anomalous under both views.

The relative allocation of evidential mass among rival intents can be atypical for OOS inputs even when total evidence is high. A class-conditioned distance on the sorted non-predicted Dirichlet concentration spectrum isolates this evidence-shape deviation.

Confident items retain energy-based ordering, while energy-uncertain items receive increasing weight from predicted-intent representation atypicality. Class-conditional distance calibration avoids over-penalizing naturally broad intents.

A shrinkage diagonal Gaussian preserves per-intent feature constraints that a tied covariance discards while remaining stable for intents with limited examples. Class-conditional calibration turns predicted-intent negative log likelihood into a comparable surprise score across naturally broad and narrow intents.

Removing the class-mean subspace suppresses directions used primarily to distinguish known intents. OOS inputs should show unusually large class-conditioned deviation in the remaining residual geometry.

ViM-style residual norm measures feature mass outside the dominant in-scope representation subspace. Treating this residual as a virtual OOS logit combines representation novelty with the classifier's native logit evidence.

OOS queries should lie in persistently sparse neighborhoods of the normalized encoder representation. Averaging several neighbor radii reduces sensitivity to isolated duplicates or a single locally dense training region.

Low-variance within-class directions encode constraints that in-scope representations should satisfy. A class-calibrated whitened deviation in this trailing subspace detects queries that violate those constraints without relying on local neighbor support.

In-scope representations should usually have a clearly preferred Gaussian intent, while OOS inputs may be similarly distant from multiple intent prototypes. The negative gap between the nearest and second-nearest class Mahalanobis distances scores this prototype ambiguity, with a small distance term breaking ties for globally remote points.

OOS queries are often assigned a known intent with a smaller gap between the two most competitive logits. Predicted-class robust calibration accounts for intents with intrinsically different logit-margin scales.

OOS queries may have weak cosine support from the class prototypes favored by the classifier, rather than merely weak support from their single closest prototype. Posterior-weighted prototype alignment incorporates disagreement among plausible known intents and changes the ordering from a maximum-cosine baseline.

Energy and full encoder-space Mahalanobis distance provide complementary logit and representation novelty signals. Smoothed train empirical-CDF log-odds put their upper tails on a common scale before additive fusion.

In-scope examples of each intent should exhibit a characteristic combination of total Dirichlet evidence, predictive concentration, and rival-intent mass. OOS inputs can be assigned a familiar class while having an atypical evidential shape for that class.
Energy remains the score for confidently in-scope-like items, while a train-calibrated predicted-intent Mahalanobis tail score increasingly dominates when energy indicates uncertainty.

A shrunk diagonal covariance preserves intent-specific feature variance while borrowing strength from the pooled distribution for small classes. OOS queries forced into a known intent should have unusually high class-calibrated surprise under their predicted intent.

Class-mean directions primarily encode distinctions among known intents, so removing them leaves residual variation that should capture within-intent constraints. OOS queries may have sparse local support in this nondiscriminative residual geometry even when their nearest intent is confident.

Feature mass outside the dominant in-scope principal subspace is a ViM-style novelty signal, since in-scope encoder outputs should concentrate near that subspace. Train-calibrated residual magnitude is added to energy so classifier uncertainty and representation-space novelty reinforce one another.

Queries confidently assigned to a known intent should still have multi-scale local support among training examples of that predicted intent. Averaging several neighbor radii reduces sensitivity to isolated duplicates while classwise train calibration accounts for different intent spread.

Low-variance within-intent directions encode tight representation constraints. Rather than summing residual energy, this score detects the largest standardized trailing-direction violation for the classifier-predicted intent.

A query can be close to some known intent while still being geometrically incompatible with the intent selected by the classifier. Calibrating predicted-intent Mahalanobis distance using that intent's training distribution accounts for naturally different class spreads.

OOS queries often have a weak separation between the two most competitive known intents. Predicted-class train calibration makes top-two margins comparable across intents with different intrinsic confidence scales.

Maximum softmax uncertainty and bottleneck-space distance capture complementary classifier and representation novelty signals. Robust train-fitted median/IQR scaling places both signals on a common bounded scale without using evaluation-set statistics.

Dirichlet mutual information measures disagreement induced by the full concentration shape, separating epistemically ambiguous predictions from merely low-energy ones. Predicted-intent robust calibration flags evidence shapes atypical for the intent selected by the classifier.
Energy is retained for confidently in-scope-like queries, while a train-calibrated local encoder-neighborhood distance is activated mainly for energy-uncertain queries.

A classifier-selected intent should agree with a shrunk diagonal class-density model. OOS queries can create disagreement between the logit-selected intent and the most geometrically compatible intent, while distance from every class resolves remote ties.

The span of class means contains directions most useful for separating known intents, so OOS inputs may violate class-conditional constraints in its orthogonal residual space. Predicted-intent calibration makes residual surprise comparable across intents.

A ViM-style residual norm measures feature mass outside the dominant in-scope encoder subspace. OOS inputs can remain logit-confident while violating the low-dimensional structure shared by training queries.

Local outlier factor compares a query's neighborhood density with the densities of its nearby in-scope neighbors, detecting OOS queries that lie in sparse or locally inconsistent regions. PCA-compressed, L2-normalized pooled embeddings emphasize semantic direction while reducing noise.

Trailing within-class covariance directions encode tight feature constraints that are weakly represented by total Mahalanobis distance. OOS inputs may produce one or a few unusually large standardized violations in these low-variance directions, so a top-order tail statistic emphasizes localized constraint failures.

OOS queries can be both far from all known intents and geometrically ambiguous between multiple class means. A train-calibrated ratio of nearest-class distance to the nearest-vs-runner-up gap emphasizes this joint failure mode.

The centered logit norm measures how strongly the classifier concentrates evidence across intents, independently of the common logit offset used by energy. OOS inputs often have unusually weak class-specific logit concentration even when their maximum probability is not extreme.

In-scope queries should align with the prototype of the intent selected by the classifier, while OOS queries can have an atypically weak predicted-intent cosine similarity. A disagreement penalty also flags cases where a different intent prototype is geometrically more compatible than the logit-selected intent.

Maximum-softmax uncertainty and bottleneck-space distance capture complementary failures: uncertain class assignment and geometric departure from known-intent representations. Train empirical-CDF calibration enables a nonlinear soft-OR fusion that emphasizes either strong novelty signal without using evaluation-set statistics.
